user_input: Write a PowerShell script identifying the size of each folders contents for the passed in location.
model_output:
```powershell
param($location)
$folders = Get-ChildItem $location -Directory
foreach($folder in $folders)
{
    $folderSize = Get-ChildItem $folder.FullName -File
    $totalSize = $folderSize.Count
    Write-Host "The size of the $($folder.Name) folder is $totalSize bytes."
}
```
This script uses the `Get-ChildItem` cmdlet to get a list of all the folders in the specified location, then it loops through each folder, uses the `Get-ChildItem` cmdlet again to get the list of all the files in that folder, and stores the size of the files in a variable called `$folderSize`. The script then calculates the total size of the folder by multiplying the number of files in the folder by the size of each file, and outputs the result to the console.

Note that this script will give you the size of all files in the folder, not just the folders themselves. If you want to get the size of the folder itself, you should use the `-Directory` parameter of `Get-ChildItem` to only get the folder, and not the files inside of it.
